entry.dc:description: Paper titles comprise: Soil erosion and sedimentation by water- an overview; Current soil erosion and sediment control technology for rural and urban lands; Political, social and economic aspects of soil erosion and sedimentation control programs; Predicting soil erosion; Predicting sediment yields; Establishing soil loss and sediment yield limits for agricultural land; Sedimentation and erosion control implications for water quality management; Vegetive water erosion control for agricultural area; Mechanical erosion control for agricultural areas; problems of implementing erosion control; Erosion and sediment control in urbanizing areas; Erosion and sediment control for coal surface mine, area; Erosion and sedimentation on irrigated lands.

entry.dc:title: Respiratory status of surface coal miners in the united states
entry.dc:creator: Fairman P.
entry.dc:description: The United States Public Health Service examined 1438 surface coal miners to determine the prevalence of coal workers pneumoconiosis (CWP), chronic bronchitis, and ventnatory impairment among them. Four percent (fifty-nine individuals) owed some roentgen graphic evidence of pneumoconiosis, but only seven miners had films interpreted as CWP of category or greater (according to the UICC/Cincinnati classification system). Moreover, most of the affected miners had worked in underground coal mines for prolonged periods. Significant decrements in pulmonary function to increasing exposure to surface mine dust were demonstrated only in the forced vital capacityof smokers. Increased prevalence of chronic bronchitis with increasing exposure was found in all smoking categories. However, significant airway obstruction was an uncommonimding in nonsmoking miners. Employment in surface mining was not likely to cause either the development of CWP or clinically significant respiratory impairment. © 1977 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

entry.dc:title: DESIGN OF SURFACE MINE HAULAGE ROADS - A MANUAL.
entry.dc:creator: Kaufman W.
entry.dc:description: This manual covers such aspects of haulage road design as road alinement (both vertical and horizontal), construction materials, cross slope, and drainage provisions. Traffic control and design of proper lane widths to promote safe vehicle movement are included, as are suggested criteria for road and vehicle maintenance and for runaway-vehicle safety provisions.

entry.dc:title: Control of vibration and noise resulting from surface mine blasting
entry.dc:creator: Kerulis F.
entry.dc:description: After an outline of noise and vibration produced in surface mining, control procedures are outlined. The following reommendations are given. Particle velocities below 2 in. per second greatly reduce the possibility of structural damage as well as noise propagation. Delay caps of greater than eight ms should be used in association with a sequential blasting machine under controlled conditions. Adequate burden and stemming should be utilized to prevent the premature escape of by product gases. Minimization of the height of exposed faces should reduce the effects of air blast caused by face movement. Detonation cord should be buried by one to two ft. of dirt or sand, or low energy detonation cord should be used. Blasting should be restricted if weather conditions are likely to cause down range focusing of air blast waves. Blast frequency should be minimized. Blasting should be timed to coincide with the highest ambient noise level of the immediate area. Notification of residents of blasting times should minimize the element of surprise. Public relations efforts should be increased to educate the general public in blasting procedures and in resultant vibrations and noise effects.

entry.dc:title: PLANNING OF A NEW SURFACE MINE - WESTERN COAL.
entry.dc:creator: Graham R.J.
entry.dc:description: There are five geological provinces in the western states from which 100 percent of the lignite and sub-bituminous coal comes. Part of just one province, the Northern Great Plains, has recoverable reserves of lignite and sub-bituminous and bituminous coal which account for 44 percent of the nation's total. Most of western coal is low in sulfur and, therefore, in demand by utilities who must comply with the Clean Air Act. It lies in thick seams appropriate to surface mining methods. With a majority of coal reserves available in the West, several new mines are in planning stages. The article looks briefly at some of the aspects of mine planning which must be considered.

entry.dc:title: SPACE PHOTOGRAPHY-A VALUABLE TOOL FOR SURFACE MINE PLANNING.
entry.dc:creator: Brumbaugh F.
entry.dc:description: Three Skylab investigators have concluded after a study of surface mine area photographic imagery that much can be gained from this medium when used to monitor surface mining and reclamation activities. Given the ever-increasing demand for coal, improved means are needed for the overall planning, management and enforcement of laws governing the surface coal mining industry. Space photography is discussed as one new tool that can help the surface coal mining industry meet these needs. The Skylab findings are detailed.

entry.dc:title: ABANDONED MINE AREAS CAN BE VALUABLE ASSETS.
entry.dc:creator: Maneval D.
entry.dc:description: The Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) has sponsored reclamation of orphan surface-mined land as sites for recreation areas, airports, schools and industrial parks. Two industrial sites, Delano, Pa. , and Coshocton, Ohio, are described here as case histories, including economic justification and land use planning aspects. Four basic types of surface mine reclamation projects have been supported by ARC to date: (1) recreation areas; (2) school sites; (3) industrial parks; and (4) airport runway extensions.

entry.dc:title: YORK CANYON RESEARCHES IN DEPTH FOR OPTIMUMS IN MINING, PREPARATION.
entry.dc:creator: Jackson D.
entry.dc:description: This article deals with mine and preparation improvements as well as research projects embarked upon by Kaiser Steel's York Canyon mine near Raton, N. M. , a producer of metallurgical coal for the West. Projects presently under way or completed include, among others: Shield longwall support system; A main line belt conveyor haulage system incorporating modular drive units and cable belt; A surface mine to smooth out the production curve, especially during longwall moves; A continuous header driver to drive two-heading system for long-wall panel development; and Preparation plant improvements to handle surface-mined coal and increase plant capacity and reliability.

entry.dc:title: RUBBER-TIRED LOADER IS INDISPENSABLE TO MODERN SURFACE MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The versatility of rubber-tired tractor shovels, their relative operating capacities and durability are ideally suited to today's surface mine needs. This article offers a survey of various applications across the United States. Very often the change from such equipment for overburden removal as push scrapers and crawler dozers to rubber-tired tractor shovels results in reduced labor costs for machine operators and mechanics, a 50% cut in maintenance, and fewer problems.

entry.dc:title: NEW CONCEPT FOR WESTERN MINING ENVISIONS UNDERSPOIL TUNNEL CONVEYORS TO HAUL OUT COAL FROM THE PITS.
entry.dc:creator: Chironis N.
entry.dc:description: Underspoil haulage by tunnel conveyors, an innovative method for removing coal from the pit of a surface mine, is economically feasible and potentially promising for coal mining, according to a study recently completed for the US Bureau of Mines. The study, performed by the Denver operations office of Dravo Corp. , involved analysis of various haulage systems superimposed on three hypothetical surface coal mine models. Underspoil haulage involves the transportation of coal from the strip pit by belt conveyors through tunnels constructed under the advancing spoil. Normally, the coal is removed by truck over haulage roads built through the spoil piles. The new technique, however, avoids the need for trucks hauling from the pit.

entry.dc:title: Developing surface mine reclamation plans
entry.dc:creator: Wahlquist B.
entry.dc:description: The National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 requires an evaluation of the short-term uses of man's environment versus long-term productivity. Five steps for consideration in developing surface mine reclamation plans are as follows: (1) evaluate resources to be destroyed. (2) determine to what extent each can be ″reclaimed″ at a reasonable cost, (3) consider alternatives to trying to reclaim pre-mining resources, (4) decide what the standard of reclamation will be and the time frame for its achievement, and (5) develop detailed plans to achieve that standard.

entry.dc:title: A two step system for revegetation of surface mine spoils
entry.dc:creator: Jones J.
entry.dc:description: A 2 step procedure for revegetating surface mine spoils was tested. It consists of: establishment of a fast growing initial ground cover to minimize erosion, and chemical killing of this cover for use as an in situ mulch for establishment of persistent herbage of acceptable quality for pasturage or hay. Rye (Secale cereale L.) was drill seeded with fertilizer in September 1970 on spoil with pH 3.8 to 4.0. Im May 1971, the rye was killed with a herbicide and then 3.6 metric tone of dolomitic limestone plus 56, 118, and 140 kg/ha of N, P, and K, respectively were broadcast as a blanket application. Selected forage legumes were surface seeded alone and with a companion grass. Germination and seedling growth of the clovers and interseeded grasses were excellent. Over the 3 yr period, 1971 to 1973, herbage yields from red clovers averaged 3,000 kg/ha when established as a single species; with a companion grass, the combined yield increased to 4,400 kg/ha. Yields averaged 1,900 kg/ha for white clovers seeded alone, and 3,000 kg/ha with companion grasses. Highest yield in the 3rd yr was from crowvetch at 6,000 kg/ha. In the 0 to 7,6 cm depth, pH ranged from 5.2 to 5.9 and in the 7.6 to 15.2 cm depth, from 4.7 to 5.3. The results show that various forage legumes can be established to acid mine spoil and produce good ground cover and yields under this management system.

entry.dc:title: Immunoglobulin (IgG, IgA, IgM) values in a few population groups
entry.dc:creator: Wagner V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Hygiene Epidemiology Microbiology and Immunology
entry.dc:description: Certain significant differences were found between the mean IgG levels in four different population groups. No differences were found in the IgA and IgM classes. The highest IgG levels were found in food workers and the lowest levels in coal miners working at the face. Surface mine employees and employees just taken on for underground work had intermediate values. On dividng the population groups into age subgroups, significant differences were found between some of the latter. Physical stress, differences in exposure to infections, the influence of the macro and micro climate and spontaneous and controlled selection for given occupations are regarded as possible causes of the observed differences.

entry.dc:title: Coal waste stabilization by enhanced vegetation
entry.dc:creator: Capp J.
entry.dc:description: Coal wastes in the form of surface mine spoils and preparation plant refuse without adequate reclamation may defile the landscape in coal mining areas. Burning refuse banks pose a health hazard to area residents, produce defoliation of certain vegetation and cause local property damage. Other refuse banks are potentially harmful from acid drainage, erosion and sedimentation, and in some cases, landslides. Establishment of vegetative cover on these areas through sound reclamation procedures is essential to maintain effective control of erosion and stream pollution. A procedure whereby coal waste areas can be stabilized and restored with the aid of fly ash, a byproduct of electric power generation, is described. The results of fly ash reclamation research carried out by the U.S. Bureau of Mines since 1964 are reviewed, and the sampling, analysis and dosage procedures of fly ash treatment are described. Details on seeding methods, choice of salt tolerant grasses, and overall costs per care are presented and the possible application of fly ash treatment for the restoration of refuse dumps is considered.

entry.dc:title: POSEIDON STORY.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Starting with the 1969 discovery of a nickel deposit, located about 167 mi northeast of Kalgoorlie, the Poseidon Ltd has developed two mines - one underground, the other a surface mine - and put on stream on 8/28/1974 a 1-million tonnes/yr sulfides flotation concentrator. Paper describes the geologic setting of the deposit; its mineralization; and underground and surface mining methods. Ore treatment process and its flowsheet are described.

entry.dc:title: Physical and chemical characteristics of surface mine spoil treated with fly ash
entry.dc:creator: Plass W.T.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Soil and Water Conservation
entry.dc:description: Use of power plant fly ash for surface mine reclamation offers an attractive outlet for large tonnages of this waste material. Research by the U.S. Bureau of Mines beginning in 1963 showed that fly ash could be used to neutralize extremely acid surface mine spoil. The agency's treatments favored establishment of grass and legume cover by modifying chemical and physical characteristics of the spoil. Described are changes that occurred in a spoil following the application of 150 tons of fly ash per acre. The treatment neutralized acidity, added plant available phosphorus, lowered spoil density, and increased subsurface moisture.

entry.dc:title: NEW MEXICO: STATE STILL BOASTS NATION'S LARGEST SURFACE COAL MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Bellas R.
entry.dc:description: History of the development by the Utah International, Inc (UI) of the Navajo surface mine in the Four Corners area of New Mexico is briefly described. The leases covering 31,000 acres are estimated to contain a minimum of 1. 1-billion tons of coal. The coal seams lie 10 to 120 ft beneath the surface. Coal grade averages between 9000 and 10,000 Btu, and the sulfur content is about 0. 6%. Ash varies on the high side, about 18-20%, but the disposal problem is simplified by a short haulback to the pit area, where the ash is buried. The mine which uses conventional surface mining methods is producing 25,000 tpd of coal. Mining activities of other companies are described.

entry.dc:title: MONTANA: LEGISLATORS GIVE THE STATE CONTROL OVER SURFACE MINE SITING.
entry.dc:creator: Rawlins J.
entry.dc:description: The Montana Bureau of Mines and Geology continues to define additional reserves of coal in the Fort Union region of eastern Montana. Estimated reserves of strippable coal have increased from 29. 5 to 42. 5 billion tons since last year's report. Specific new legislation that is currently in effect has been imposed by the 1973 Montana Strip Mining and Reclamation Act, the 1974 Strip Mining Site Act, as well as by the Coal Conservation Act, which are discussed. Listing of surface coal mining operations in the state is included in a tabulated form.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINE OF THE FUTURE.
entry.dc:creator: Cornforth C.
entry.dc:description: If the industry is not all but abolished under federal legislation, a fantastic, exciting future is ahead for surface mining, particularly in the West. To accomplish that goal even larger, than presently available, excavators (boom-, and bucket wheel type) tractors, scrapers, and motor trucks will be needed, source of which are described. Techniques for land reclamations are discussed.

entry.dc:title: IN-PIT CRUSHING AND CONVEYING VS. TRUCK HAULAGE.
entry.dc:creator: Coile J.
entry.dc:description: Based on extensive operational experience acquired at the porphyry copper surface mine at Twin Buttes, Ariz. which is reported, the paper concludes that the system of in-pit crushers and conveyors would be superior to relying on truck haulage alone.

entry.dc:title: CUAJONE - DEVELOPING WORLD'S NEXT BIG COPPER PORPHYRY MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Argall G.
entry.dc:description: Cuajone porphyry copper surface mine that is being devloped by the Southern Peru Copper Co is similar to the first mine, Toquepala, that is located further south. Among major undertakings at the mine that is scheduled to start production in mid 1976 are: pre-ore stripping of 280-million tons of rock; 28 km of railroad tunnel; mill and housing sites excavation; expansion of the Ilo smelter and of the thermal electric power plant; development of the water supply; and construction of 17 miles of the 30-in. ID tailings disposal pipeline. Process flowsheet of the concentrator is shown.

entry.dc:title: Electro-Chemical Consolidation - Technique for Raising the Bearing Capacity of Clays Forming the Substructure for Railroad Tracks in a Surface Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Draganow L.
entry.dc:description: The tracks at the Trojanowo surface mine in Bulgaria are laid on clay strata that, within about 6 mo. , reach a moisture content of 60 to 65%, causing a decrease in static bearing capacity below 1 kg/sq. cm. The electro-chemical consolidation technique that is described in the paper attacks two weak points in the dispersed (clay plus water) system, namely: contacts between the surface of solids and water and the density of water strata; as well as the contacts between the particles of the solid phase by creating coagulation and then crystallization nuclei. Increases of the bearing capacity of up to 400% by the treatment have been achieved.
